articles.title: 完型 · 拉丁美洲独立后的政治理想与现实
articles.context: 历史叙述与制度分析。先交代拉美独立后的政治理想，再转向宗教、奴隶制与民主准备不足的现实张力；稳定、清楚，转折处有分量。
rows: By 1830, the former Spanish and Portuguese colonies had become independent nations.
到1830年，原先的西班牙和葡萄牙殖民地已经成为独立国家。
The roughly 20 million inhabitants of these nations looked hopefully to the future.
这些国家大约两千万居民满怀希望地展望未来。

Born in the crisis of the old regime and Iberian colonialism, many of the leaders of independence shared the ideals of representative government, careers open to talent, freedom of commerce and trade, the right to private property, and a belief in the individual as the basis of society.
许多独立运动领袖诞生于旧制度与伊比利亚殖民统治的危机之中，他们共同信奉一系列理想：代议制政府、凭才干获得职业机会、商业与贸易自由、私人财产权，以及把个人视为社会基础的观念。
Generally, there was a belief that the new nations should be sovereign and independent states, large enough to be economically viable and integrated by a common set of laws.
总体而言，人们相信这些新国家应当成为拥有主权的独立国家，规模要大到足以在经济上自立，并由一套共同法律整合起来。
On the issue of freedom of religion and the position of the Church, however, there was less agreement among the leadership.
然而，在宗教自由和教会地位的问题上，领导层内部的共识就少得多。
Roman Catholicism had been the state religion and the only one allowed by the Spanish crown.
罗马天主教原本是国教，也是西班牙王室唯一允许的宗教。
While most leaders sought to maintain Catholicism as the official religion of the new states, some sought to end the exclusion of other faiths.
虽然大多数领导人希望继续把天主教维持为新国家的官方宗教，但也有人主张结束对其他信仰的排斥。
The defense of the Church became a rallying cry for the conservative forces.
捍卫教会由此成为保守势力的号召口号。
The ideals of the early leaders of independence were often egalitarian, valuing equality of everything.
早期独立运动领袖的理想往往带有平等主义色彩，强调各方面的平等。
Bolivar had received aid from Haiti and had promised in return to abolish slavery in the areas he liberated.
玻利瓦尔曾得到海地援助，并承诺作为回报，在自己解放的地区废除奴隶制。
By 1854, slavery had been abolished everywhere except Spain's remaining colonies.
到1854年，除西班牙仍保有的殖民地外，奴隶制已在各地被废除。
Early promises to end Indian tribute and taxes on people of mixed origin came much slower because the new nations still needed the revenue such policies produced.
早期关于取消印第安人贡赋以及废除混血人口税收的承诺，落实得要慢得多，因为这些新国家仍需要这些政策带来的财政收入。
Egalitarian sentiments were often tempered by fears that the mass of the population was unprepared for self-rule and democracy.
平等主义情怀也常常受到一种担忧的制约：人们害怕广大民众尚未准备好实行自治与民主。

articles.title: 阅读一 · 顶尖表现是练出来的
articles.context: 能力发展与刻意练习主题。由世界杯球员出生月份现象切入，以 Ericsson 的记忆训练研究说明专家表现更多来自刻意练习；结论处强调天赋被高估，以及专家是练出来的而非天生的。
rows: If you were to examine the birth certificates of every soccer player in 2006's World Cup tournament, you would most likely find a noteworthy quirk: elite soccer players are more likely to have been born in the earlier months of the year than in the later months.
如果查看2006年世界杯所有足球运动员的出生证明，你很可能会发现一个值得注意的反常现象：顶尖足球运动员出生在年初几个月的概率，比出生在年末几个月更高。
If you then examined the European national youth teams that feed the World Cup and professional ranks, you would find this strange phenomenon to be even more pronounced.
如果再查看那些为世界杯和职业联赛输送球员的欧洲国家青年队，你会发现这种奇怪现象更加明显。
What might account for this strange phenomenon?
这种奇怪现象究竟该如何解释？

Here are a few guesses: a) certain astrological signs confer superior soccer skills; b) winter-born babies tend to have higher oxygen capacity, which increases soccer stamina; c) soccer-mad parents are more likely to conceive children in springtime, at the annual peak of soccer mania; d) none of the above.
这里有几种猜测：某些星座会赋予人更强的足球技能；冬季出生的婴儿往往有更高的携氧能力，从而增强足球耐力；痴迷足球的父母更可能在春季孕育孩子，那正是一年中足球狂热的高峰；或者，以上说法都不对。
Anders Ericsson, a 58-year-old psychology professor at Florida State University, says he believes strongly in "none of the above."
佛罗里达州立大学58岁的心理学教授安德斯·埃里克森说，他坚信答案是“以上都不对”。
Ericsson grew up in Sweden, and studied nuclear engineering until he realized he would have more opportunity to conduct his own research if he switched to psychology.
埃里克森在瑞典长大，最初学习核工程，后来意识到，如果转到心理学领域，他会有更多机会开展自己的研究。
His first experiment, nearly 30 years ago, involved memory: training a person to hear and then repeat a random series of numbers.
大约30年前，他的第一个实验研究的是记忆：训练一个人听取一串随机数字，然后把它们复述出来。
“With the first subject, after about 20 hours of training, his digit span had risen from 7 to 20,” Ericsson recalls.
埃里克森回忆说：“第一名受试者经过大约20小时训练后，数字记忆广度从7位提高到了20位。”
"He kept improving, and after about 200 hours of training he had risen to over 80 numbers."
“他还在不断进步，训练大约200小时后，已经能够记住80多个数字。”

This success, coupled with later research showing that memory itself is not genetically determined, led Ericsson to conclude that the act of memorizing is more of a cognitive exercise than an intuitive one.
这一成功，加上后来表明记忆本身并非由遗传决定的研究，使埃里克森得出结论：记忆行为与其说是一种直觉活动，不如说是一种认知练习。
In other words, whatever inborn differences two people may exhibit in their abilities to memorize, those differences are swamped by how well each person "encodes" the information.
换句话说，不管两个人天生的记忆能力存在什么差异，这些差异都会被各自对信息进行“编码”的能力所淹没。
And the best way to learn how to encode information meaningfully, Ericsson determined, was a process known as deliberate practice.
埃里克森认为，学会如何有意义地编码信息，最好的办法是一种被称为“刻意练习”的过程。
Deliberate practice entails more than simply repeating a task.
刻意练习绝不只是简单地重复一项任务。
Rather, it involves setting specific goals, obtaining immediate feedback and concentrating as much on technique as on outcome.
它要求设定具体目标、获得即时反馈，并且对技术方法投入不亚于对结果的关注。
Ericsson and his colleagues have thus taken to studying expert performers in a wide range of pursuits, including soccer.
因此，埃里克森及其同事开始研究包括足球在内的众多领域中的顶尖表现者。
They gather all the data they can, not just performance statistics and biographical details but also the results of their own laboratory experiments with high achievers.
他们尽可能收集一切数据，不仅包括成绩统计和个人经历，还包括他们在实验室中对高成就者进行实验所得的结果。
Their work makes a rather startling assertion: the trait we commonly call talent is highly overrated.
他们的研究提出了一个颇为惊人的论断：我们通常所说的“天赋”被严重高估了。
Or, put another way, expert performers— whether in memory or surgery, ballet or computer programming— are nearly always made, not born.
换一种说法，无论是在记忆、外科手术、芭蕾还是计算机编程领域，专家级表现者几乎总是后天练成的，而不是天生的。

articles.title: 阅读二 · IQ 测试能测出什么
articles.context: 认知与测量主题。先借 Marilyn vos Savant 的高 IQ 与现实问题形成反差，再解释 IQ 测试的形式、计分变化和预测边界；保持学术清晰，对‘测试分数不等于全部智能’这一中心观点加强信息重音。
rows: For the past several years, the Sunday newspaper supplement Parade has featured a column called ‘Ask Marilyn.’
过去几年里，周日报纸增刊《Parade》一直设有一个名为“Ask Marilyn”的专栏。
People are invited to query Marilyn vos Savant, who at age 10 had tested at a mental level of someone about 23 years old; that gave her an IQ of 228—the highest score ever recorded.
读者可以向玛丽莲·沃斯·莎凡特提问；她10岁时测试出的心智能力相当于大约23岁的人，因此得到228的智商分数——这是有记录以来的最高分。
IQ tests ask you to complete verbal and visual analogies, to envision paper after it has been folded and cut, and to deduce numerical sequences, among other similar tasks.
智商测试会要求你完成语言和图形类比，想象纸张折叠、剪裁后的样子，并推断数字序列等。
So it is a bit confusing when vos Savant fields such queries from the average Joe (whose IQ is 100) as, ‘What's the difference between love and fondness?’
因此，当莎凡特面对普通人——其智商通常为100——提出诸如“爱与喜欢有什么区别？”这样的问题时，就多少让人感到困惑。
Or what is the nature of luck and coincidence?
或者：“运气与巧合的本质是什么？”
It's not obvious how the capacity to visualize objects and to figure out numerical patterns suits one to answer questions that have eluded some of the best poets and philosophers.
很难看出，想象物体形状和识别数字规律的能力，为什么就能使一个人适合回答那些连最优秀的诗人和哲学家都未能解决的问题。
eluded some of the best poets and philosophers
Clearly, intelligence encompasses more than a score on a test.
显然，智力所包含的内容远不止测试中的一个分数。
Just what does it mean to be smart?
那么，聪明究竟意味着什么？
what does it mean to be smart
How much of intelligence can be specified, and how much can we learn about it from neurology, genetics, computer science and other fields?
智力究竟有多少可以被明确界定？我们又能从神经学、遗传学、计算机科学及其他领域中了解它多少？
The defining term of intelligence in humans still seems to be the IQ score, even though IQ tests are not given as often as they used to be.
尽管如今智商测试已不像过去那样频繁使用，但衡量人类智力时最具代表性的指标似乎仍是 IQ 分数。
still seems to be the IQ score
The test comes primarily in two forms: the Stanford-Binet Intelligence Scale and the Wechsler Intelligence Scales (both come in adult and children's versions).
这类测试主要有两种形式：斯坦福—比奈智力量表和韦氏智力量表，两者都分别有成人版和儿童版。
Generally costing several hundred dollars, they are usually given only by psychologists, although variations of them populate bookstores and the World Wide Web.
这类测试通常费用高达数百美元，而且一般只有心理学家才能施测，尽管它们的各种变体在书店和互联网上随处可见。

Superhigh scores like vos Savant's are no longer possible, because scoring is now based on a statistical population distribution among age peers, rather than simply dividing the mental age by the chronological age and multiplying by 100.
像莎凡特那样的超高分如今已不可能出现，因为现在的计分依据是同龄人群中的统计分布，而不再只是用心理年龄除以实际年龄再乘以100。
Other standardized tests, such as the Scholastic Assessment Test (SAT) and the Graduate Record Exam (GRE), capture the main aspects of IQ tests.
其他标准化考试，如学术能力评估考试（SAT）和研究生入学考试（GRE），也涵盖了智商测试的主要方面。
Such standardized tests may not assess all the important elements necessary to succeed in school and in life, argues Robert J. Sternberg.
罗伯特·J·斯滕伯格指出，这类标准化测试未必能评估一个人在学校和生活中取得成功所需要的全部重要因素。
succeed in school and in life

In his article ‘How Intelligent Is Intelligence Testing?’, Sternberg notes that traditional tests best assess analytical and verbal skills but fail to measure creativity and practical knowledge, components also critical to problem solving and life success.
斯滕伯格在《智力测试究竟有多“智能”？》一文中指出，传统测试最擅长衡量分析能力和语言能力，却无法测量创造力和实践知识，而后两者同样是解决问题和获得人生成功的关键要素。
best assess analytical and verbal skills
fail to measure creativity and practical knowledge
Moreover, IQ tests do not necessarily predict so well once populations or situations change.
此外，一旦受测人群或情境发生变化，智商测试的预测效果就未必那么可靠。
do not necessarily predict so well

Research has found that IQ predicted leadership skills when the tests were given under low-stress conditions, but under high-stress conditions, IQ was negatively correlated with leadership—that is, it predicted the opposite.
研究发现，在低压力条件下进行测试时，IQ 能预测领导能力；但在高压力条件下，IQ 与领导能力却呈负相关——也就是说，它预测出了相反的结果。
Anyone who has toiled through SAT will testify that test-taking skill also matters, whether it's knowing when to guess or what questions to skip.
任何苦熬过 SAT 的人都会证明，应试技巧同样重要，比如知道什么时候该猜、哪些题该跳过。

articles.title: 阅读三 · 中产家庭承担的金融风险
articles.context: 经济与家庭风险分析。核心不是煽情，而是解释双职工家庭、退休、医疗和人口结构如何把风险逐步转移给中产家庭；语气理性、克制，但末段政治后果要形成明显收束。
rows: During the past generation, the American middle-class family that once could count on hard work and fair play to keep itself financially secure has been transformed by economic risk and new realities.
在过去一代人的时间里，美国中产家庭曾经可以依靠勤奋工作和公平竞争来维持经济安全，如今却已被经济风险和新的现实彻底改变。
Now a pink slip, a bad diagnosis, or a disappearing spouse can reduce a family from solidly middle class to newly poor in a few months.
如今，一纸解雇通知、一份糟糕的诊断结果，或配偶的离去，都可能在短短几个月内让一个原本稳居中产的家庭沦为新贫困家庭。
In just one generation, millions of mothers have gone to work, transforming basic family economics.
仅仅一代人的时间里，数以百万计的母亲走入职场，从根本上改变了家庭经济结构。
Scholars, policymakers, and critics of all stripes have debated the social implications of these changes, but few have looked at the side effect: family risk has risen as well.
学者、政策制定者以及各种立场的评论人士一直在争论这些变化的社会影响，却很少有人注意到一个副作用：家庭面临的风险也上升了。
Today's families have budgeted to the limits of their new two-paycheck status.
如今的家庭已经把两份工资收入几乎全部纳入日常预算，开支逼近了双收入所能承受的极限。
As a result, they have lost the parachute they once had in times of financial setback—a back-up earner, usually Mom, who could go into the workforce if the primary earner got laid off or fell sick.
结果，一旦遭遇经济挫折，他们失去了过去那把“降落伞”——一名备用挣钱者，通常是母亲；当主要收入者被裁员或生病时，她原本可以进入劳动力市场补上收入缺口。
This added-worker effect could support the safety net offered by unemployment insurance or disability insurance to help families weather bad times.
这种“新增劳动者效应”原本可以与失业保险或伤残保险提供的安全网相互补充，帮助家庭熬过困难时期。
But today, a disruption to family fortunes can no longer be made up with extra income from an otherwise-stay-at-home partner.
但在今天，家庭经济一旦遭受冲击，已经无法再靠原本留在家中的配偶额外就业来弥补损失。
can no longer be made up
During the same period, families have been asked to absorb much more risk in their retirement income.
与此同时，家庭还被要求自行承担更多退休收入方面的风险。

Steelworkers, airline employees, and now those in the auto industry are joining millions of families who must worry about interest rates, stock market fluctuation, and the harsh reality that they may outlive their retirement money.
钢铁工人、航空公司雇员，如今再加上汽车业从业者，正加入数以百万计家庭的行列：他们必须担忧利率、股市波动，以及一个残酷现实——自己可能活得比退休储蓄更久。

For much of the past year, President Bush campaigned to move Social Security to a savings-account model, with retirees trading much or all of their guaranteed payments for payments depending on investment returns.
在过去一年的大部分时间里，布什总统一直推动把社会保障制度改成储蓄账户模式，让退休者用原本全部或大部分有保障的给付，换取取决于投资回报的收入。
For younger families, the picture is not any better.
对更年轻的家庭来说，情况也没有好到哪里去。

Both the absolute cost of healthcare and the share of it borne by families have risen—and newly fashionable health-savings plans are spreading from legislative halls to Wal-Mart workers, with much higher deductibles and a large new dose of investment risk for families' future healthcare.
医疗总成本以及由家庭承担的那部分费用都在上升；与此同时，新近流行的医疗储蓄计划正从立法机构扩展到沃尔玛员工，而这类计划伴随着高得多的免赔额，也把一大块新的投资风险转嫁给家庭未来的医疗保障。

Even demographics are working against the middle-class family, as the odds of having a weak elderly parent—and all the attendant need for physical and financial assistance—have jumped eightfold in just one generation.
甚至人口结构也在对中产家庭不利：仅仅一代人的时间里，家中出现体弱年迈父母的概率已经增加到原来的八倍，随之而来的还有身体照护和经济援助需求。

From the middle-class family perspective, much of this, understandably, looks far less like an opportunity to exercise more financial responsibility, and a good deal more like a frightening acceleration of the wholesale shift of financial risk onto their already overburdened shoulders.
从中产家庭的角度看，这一切当然不像是一次承担更多财务责任的机会，反而更像是一场令人恐惧的加速过程：金融风险正在大规模转移到他们本已不堪重负的肩上。
The financial fallout has begun, and the political fallout may not be far behind.
经济上的后果已经显现，而政治上的后果恐怕也不会太远。

articles.title: 阅读四 · 数据泄露与企业治理
articles.context: 公司治理与监管评论。先以企业连续遭遇麻烦切入，再把数据安全提升为董事会和管理层责任，最后落到立法与监管。语气权威、克制，关键论断要清晰有压重。
rows: It never rains but it pours.

Just as bosses and boards have finally sorted out their worst accounting and compliance troubles, and improved their feeble corporate governance, a new problem threatens to earn them—especially in America—the sort of nasty headlines that inevitably lead to heads rolling in the executive suite: data insecurity.
就在企业老板和董事会终于处理好最严重的会计与合规问题，并改善了原本薄弱的公司治理之际，一个新的问题又威胁着他们——尤其是在美国——它足以招来那种最终导致高管下台的负面头条：数据安全失守。

Left, until now, to odd, low-level IT staff to put right, and seen as a concern only of data-rich industries such as banking, telecoms and air travel, information protection is now high on the boss's agenda in businesses of every variety.
过去，信息保护往往被丢给边缘、低层级的 IT 员工处理，也只被视为银行、电信和航空等数据密集行业才需要担心的问题；如今，它已经进入各类企业老板的核心议程。
now high on the boss's agenda

Several massive leakages of customer and employee data this year—from organizations as diverse as Time Warner, the American defense contractor Science Applications International Corp and even the University of California, Berkeley—have left managers hurriedly peering into their intricate IT systems and business processes in search of potential vulnerabilities.
今年，多家背景迥异的机构发生了大规模客户和员工数据泄露，从时代华纳、美国国防承包商 Science Applications International Corp，甚至到加州大学伯克利分校；这些事件迫使管理者匆忙检查复杂的 IT 系统和业务流程，寻找潜在漏洞。
“Data is becoming an asset which needs to be guarded as much as any other asset,” says Haim Mendelson of Stanford University's business school.
斯坦福大学商学院的 Haim Mendelson 说：“数据正在变成一种资产，需要像保护其他任何资产一样加以保护。”
“The ability to guard customer data is the key to market value, which the board is responsible for on behalf of shareholders.”
“保护客户数据的能力关系到企业的市场价值，而董事会要代表股东对此负责。”

Indeed, just as there is the concept of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, perhaps it is time for GASP, Generally Accepted Security Practices, suggested Eli Noam of New York's Columbia Business School.
纽约哥伦比亚大学商学院的 Eli Noam 指出，既然有“公认会计原则”（GAAP）这一概念，也许现在该有一套“公认安全实践”（GASP）了。
“Setting the proper investment level for security, redundancy, and recovery is a management issue, not a technical one,” he says.
他说：“为安全、冗余和恢复确定适当的投入水平，是一个管理问题，而不是一个技术问题。”
The mystery is that this should come as a surprise to any boss.
令人费解的是，这种道理竟然还会让某些老板感到意外。

Surely it should be obvious to the dimmest executive that trust, that most valuable of economic assets, is easily destroyed and hugely expensive to restore—and that few things are more likely to destroy trust than a company letting sensitive personal data get into the wrong hands.
即便是最迟钝的企业高管也理应明白：信任这种最宝贵的经济资产极易被毁掉，而重建成本却高得惊人；几乎没有什么比企业让敏感个人数据落入错误之手更容易摧毁信任。
The current state of affairs may have been encouraged—though not justified—by the lack of legal penalty in America, but not Europe, for data leakage.
目前这种局面或许受到一个因素的纵容——尽管这并不能为其辩解——那就是美国对数据泄露缺乏法律惩罚，而欧洲并非如此。
Until California recently passed a law, American firms did not have to tell anyone, even the victim, when data went astray.
直到加州最近通过一项法律之前，美国公司即使发生数据失窃，也无须告知任何人，甚至不必通知受害者本人。
did not have to tell anyone
That may change fast: lots of proposed data-security legislation is now doing the rounds in Washington, D.C.
这种情况可能很快改变：目前华盛顿正在流转、讨论大量拟议中的数据安全立法。

Meanwhile, the theft of information about some 40 million credit-card accounts in America, disclosed on June 17th, overshadowed a hugely important decision a day earlier by America's Federal Trade Commission that puts corporate America on notice that regulators will act if firms fail to provide adequate data security.
与此同时，6月17日披露的一起涉及美国约四千万个信用卡账户的信息盗窃案，盖过了前一天美国联邦贸易委员会作出的一项极其重要的决定；这项决定实际上是在警告美国企业界：如果公司不能提供充分的数据安全保障，监管者就会采取行动。

articles.title: 新题型 · 父母如何帮助孩子走向成年
articles.context: 面向父母的实用建议文。语气成熟、温和、有经验感；每组建议都像面对面解释，不朗诵标题。A-G 标题、41-45 编号和Directions全部排除，只保留文章真实正文。
rows: Mothers and fathers can do a lot to ensure a safe landing in early adulthood for their kids.
父母可以做很多事情，帮助孩子平稳地进入成年早期。

Even if a job's starting salary seems too small to satisfy an emerging adult's need for rapid content, the transition from school to work can be less of a setback if the start-up adult is ready for the move.
即使一份工作的起薪看起来不足以满足一个初入成年的年轻人对迅速获得满足的期待，只要这个刚起步的成年人为转变做好了准备，从学校走向职场就不会那么像一次挫折。
Here are a few measures, drawn from my book Ready or Not? Here Life Comes, that parents can take to prevent what I call “work-life unreadiness”:
下面这些做法摘自我的书《准备好了吗？生活来了》，父母可以借此预防我所说的“工作与生活准备不足”。
You can start this process when they are 11 or 12.
孩子十一二岁时，你就可以开始这个过程。
Periodically review their emerging strengths and weaknesses with them and work together on any shortcomings, like difficulty in communicating well or collaborating.
定期和孩子一起审视逐渐显现出来的优势与弱点，并共同改善不足之处，例如不善沟通或协作。
Also, identify the kinds of interests they keep coming back to, as these offer clues to the careers that will fit them best.
同时，留意那些他们总会反复回到的兴趣，因为这些兴趣会为最适合他们的职业提供线索。
Kids need a range of authentic role models—as opposed to members of their clique, pop stars and vaunted athletes.
孩子需要一系列真实可信的榜样，而不是只盯着朋友圈里的同伴、流行明星或被吹捧的运动员。
Have regular dinner-table discussions about people the family knows and how they got where they are.
经常在餐桌上谈谈家里认识的人，以及他们是怎样走到今天这一步的。
how they got where they are
Discuss the joys and downsides of your own career and encourage your kids to form some ideas about their own future.
谈谈你自己职业中的乐趣和不如意，也鼓励孩子对自己的未来形成一些想法。
When asked what they want to do, they should be discouraged from saying, “I have no idea.”
当被问到以后想做什么时，不应让孩子习惯用“我不知道”来作答。
They can change their minds 200 times, but having only a foggy view of the future is of little good.
他们当然可以把想法改上两百次，但如果对未来始终只有一片模糊的印象，也没有什么好处。
Teachers are responsible for teaching kids how to learn; parents should be responsible for teaching them how to work.
教师负责教孩子怎样学习；父母则应该负责教他们怎样工作。
Assign responsibilities around the house and make sure homework deadlines are met.
给孩子分配家务责任，并确保他们按时完成作业。
Encourage teenagers to take a part-time job.
鼓励青少年去做一份兼职。
Kids need plenty of practice delaying gratification and deploying effective organizational skills, such as managing time and setting priorities.
孩子需要大量练习延迟满足，并运用有效的组织能力，比如管理时间和确定事情的优先次序。
Playing video games encourages immediate content.
玩电子游戏会强化即时满足。
And hours of watching TV shows with canned laughter only teaches kids to process information in a passive way.
长时间观看配有罐头笑声的电视节目，也只会让孩子以被动方式处理信息。
At the same time, listening through earphones to the same monotonous beats for long stretches encourages kids to stay inside their bubble instead of pursuing other endeavors.
与此同时，长时间戴着耳机反复听同样单调的节拍，也会让孩子更愿意躲在自己的小世界里，而不是去尝试其他事情。
All these activities can prevent the growth of important communication and thinking skills and make it difficult for kids to develop the kind of sustained concentration they will need for most jobs.
这些活动都可能妨碍重要沟通能力和思考能力的发展，也会让孩子难以培养大多数工作所需要的那种持久专注力。
They should know how to deal with setbacks, stresses and feelings of inadequacy.
他们应该懂得怎样应对挫折、压力和能力不足感。
They should also learn how to solve problems and resolve conflicts, ways to brainstorm and think critically.
他们还应该学会解决问题、化解冲突，以及进行头脑风暴和批判性思考的方法。
Discussions at home can help kids practice doing these things and help them apply these skills to everyday life situations.
家庭中的讨论能够帮助孩子练习这些能力，并把它们运用到日常生活情境中。
What about the son or daughter who is grown but seems to be struggling and wandering aimlessly through early adulthood?
那么，如果儿女已经长大，却似乎仍在成年早期苦苦挣扎、漫无目的地徘徊，又该怎么办呢？
Parents still have a major role to play, but now it is more delicate.
父母仍然扮演着重要角色，只是此时需要处理得更加谨慎。
They have to be careful not to come across as disappointed in their child.
他们必须注意，不要让孩子觉得父母对自己很失望。

They should exhibit strong interest and respect for whatever currently interests their fledgling adult, as naive or ill conceived as it may seem, while becoming a partner in exploring options for the future.
无论这个初入成年的孩子眼下感兴趣的事情看起来多么幼稚或考虑不周，父母都应表现出真切的兴趣和尊重，同时成为孩子探索未来选择的伙伴。
Most of all, these new adults must feel that they are respected and supported by a family that appreciates them.
最重要的是，这些刚步入成年的年轻人必须感受到：家人欣赏他们，也尊重并支持他们。

articles.title: 翻译 · 法律教育与新闻专业素养
articles.context: 法律教育与新闻专业责任。这里只保留试卷要求翻译的 46-50 五个目标译段，不扩展到整篇背景文。语气清晰、理性、正式，法律与新闻术语优先保证准确。
rows: Traditionally, legal learning has been viewed in such institutions as the special preserve of lawyers, rather than a necessary part of the intellectual equipment of an educated person.
传统上，在这些院校中，法律学习一直被视为律师这一职业群体的专属领域，而不是一个受过教育的人知识素养中必不可少的一部分。
On the other, it links these concepts to everyday realities in a manner which is parallel to the links journalists forge on a daily basis as they cover and comment on the news.
另一方面，法律又把这些概念同日常现实联系起来；这种联系方式，与记者每天在报道和评论新闻时所建立的概念与现实之间的联系是相似的。
parallel to the links journalists forge

But the idea that the journalist must understand the law more profoundly than an ordinary citizen rests on an understanding of the established conventions and special responsibilities of the news media.
但是，记者必须比普通公民更深刻地理解法律这一观点，是建立在对新闻媒体既有惯例和特殊责任的认识之上的。
In fact, it is difficult to see how journalists who do not have a clear grasp of the basic features of the Canadian Constitution can do a competent job on political stories.
事实上，很难想象，一个不能清楚掌握加拿大宪法基本特征的记者，如何能够胜任政治新闻报道。
do not have a clear grasp
While comment and reaction from lawyers may enhance stories, it is preferable for journalists to rely on their own notions of significance and make their own judgments.
尽管律师的评论和反应可能会使报道更加充实，但记者最好还是依靠自己对事件重要性的理解，并作出自己的判断。
